title: Plumbing Code Upgrade on Repaired Supply Runs by Year Built — HomeGuard Homeowners Policy
content:
When dwelling water damage on a HomeGuard Homeowners Policy claim is settled in place of a repeated-seepage denial, a plumbing code-upgrade allowance for bringing the repaired supply run to the current plumbing code is added at a percentage of the replacement-cost value of the dwelling water damage. The allowance depends on the year the dwelling was built, as shown on the declarations, and on the package's ordinance-or-law percentage.

| Year built | Package ordinance-or-law percentage | Allowance |
|---|---|---|
| before 1980 | 25 or more | 5 percent |
| before 1980 | below 25 | 3 percent |
| 1980 or later | any | none — the supply lines already meet that code |

The allowance is added to the reversal payment on the dwelling water damage before the floor at 0.00 and the single rounding to the cent, and is taken on the replacement-cost value recorded on the dwelling damage's repeated-seepage denial entry.

**Edge lines.**
- A dwelling built in 1979 is built before 1980; a dwelling built in 1980 is not.
- An ordinance-or-law percentage of exactly 25 is "25 or more" and gives 5 percent; a percentage of 24 or less gives 3 percent.

**Worked lines (hypothetical figures).** On a hypothetical replacement-cost value of 10000.00: built 1965 on a package with ordinance-or-law percentage 25, the allowance is 500.00; built 1965 on a package with ordinance-or-law percentage 10, 300.00; built 1985, nothing.

The ordinance-or-law percentage is the one the package carries in its schedule of coverages.
